name: Bhakti defined across the schools

definitions.definition: Nārada Bhakti Sūtra: supreme love (parama-prema) for the Lord, of the nature of nectar; not desire but relinquishment; its own fruit.
Śāṇḍilya Bhakti Sūtra: supreme attachment (parānurakti) to Īśvara — a form of rāga, not knowledge, not an act.
NBS 16–19's doxography: attachment to worship (Vyāsa), to hearing his stories (Garga), love not opposed to delight in the self (Śāṇḍilya), offering all acts and anguish at forgetting him (Nārada).
The Āḻvārs: love (aṉpu), longing (ārvam) and a melting heart lit as a lamp for Nāraṇaṉ; 'knowledge-and-love' (matinalam) given by the Lord's grace.
Rāmānuja: knowledge that has become love (prīti) — steady remembrance (dhruvānusmṛti) of the Lord, vivid as perception, won by his grace.
Madhva: very firm love (sneha), greater than love for anything else, preceded by knowledge of the Lord's greatness.
Rūpa Gosvāmī: pure devotion (uttamā bhakti) is favourable cultivation of Kṛṣṇa, empty of other desires and unobscured by knowledge and works.
Madhusūdana Sarasvatī: the mind melted by the Lord's qualities flowing continuously toward him; the Vivekacūḍāmaṇi: devotion is the constant search into one's own true nature.
The Bhāgavata: devotion free of the guṇas is the mind's unbroken movement toward the Lord, like the Gaṅgā to the sea, unmotivated and uninterrupted.
The Gītā: by undivided devotion the Lord is known, seen and entered; supreme devotion is reached by one who has become Brahman.

notes: Graded equivalences between the defining terms are recorded on the terms (trm:parama-prema, trm:paranurakti, trm:matinalam, trm:kanta-bhava) with rests_on. The schools do not accept each other's definitions: Advaita reads devotion as a means to or form of self-knowledge; the Nārada Sūtra holds it is the fruit; Rāmānuja makes it a form of knowledge; the Śāṇḍilya Sūtra denies that it is knowledge.

name: Devotion (bhakti)

definitions.definition: Love, longing and a melting heart for Tirumāl, given by his grace, lived as service, refuge and praise at his temples; Tamil pattu/aṉpu.
Supreme love of the nature of nectar, higher than action, knowledge and yoga, being the fruit itself; primary (one, though elevenfold) and secondary (by guṇas or motive).

name: Secondary and supreme devotion (gauṇī and parā/mukhyā bhakti)

definitions.definition: Secondary devotion is threefold, by the guṇas or by the motive (the distressed and the others), each earlier kind better; primary devotion is love itself, one though it appears in eleven forms.
Secondary devotion — singing, remembering, worship — is the cause of and leads to supreme devotion (Śāṇḍilya Sūtra, as recalled).

relations.note: gauṇī → parā compares with the Gauḍīya sādhana → bhāva → prema; the Gauḍīya scheme has an intermediate stage the sūtras do not name
the guṇa-grading of secondary devotion is the Bhāgavata's grading (BhP 3.29)

name: The eleven forms of attachment (ekādaśa-āsakti)

definitions.definition: Devotion, though one, appears as eleven attachments: to the glory of the Lord's qualities, to his form, to worship, to remembrance, to service, to friendship, to parental love, to love as a beloved, to self-offering, to absorption in him, and to supreme separation.

relations.note: five items coincide with the Bhāgavata's nine (remembrance, worship, service, friendship, self-offering)
the servant, friend, parental and beloved attachments answer to the Gauḍīya dāsya, sakhya, vātsalya and madhura rasas

notes: Order of vātsalya and kāntā differs between editions.

name: Devotion as its own fruit (phala-rūpatva)

definitions.definition: Devotion is higher than action, knowledge and yoga because it is the fruit; knowledge of a king or of food neither pleases the king nor appeases hunger; gaining devotion one becomes perfected, immortal, satisfied.

The Āḻvārs ask for nothing but service and devotion: not the drum but kinship and service through seven times seven births (TP 29); not dharma, wealth or pleasure but unwavering devotion in every birth (Mukundamālā); the name's sweetness above Indra's kingdom (Tirumālai 2).

relations.note: Advaita makes devotion a means to or a form of self-knowledge
Gauḍīya prema as the fifth aim beyond liberation states the same claim within a rasa theology

name: Relinquishment, single-mindedness and indifference (nirodha, ananyatā, udāsīnatā)

definitions.definition: Devotion is not desire, being relinquishment — the laying down of worldly and Vedic activity in the Lord; this means single-mindedness toward him (giving up other supports) and indifference to what opposes him (doing only what is favourable to him); its means include giving up sense-objects and attachment.

name: The grace and company of great souls

definitions.definition: Devotion comes chiefly by the grace of great souls or a drop of the Lord's grace; their company is hard to gain, unfathomable and unfailing, and is itself gained by his grace, for there is no difference between him and his people.
The Āḻvārs seek the company and service of devotees: the Tiruppāvai's girls wake one another before approaching the Lord; Kulaśekhara longs for the devotees of Śrīraṅgam.

name: The qualities of the devotee

definitions.definition: Humility (the Lord dislikes pride), non-violence, truth, purity, compassion and faith; no disputation; no attention to talk of lust, wealth, unbelievers and enemies; all conduct offered to the Lord; among devotees no distinction of caste, learning, beauty, family, wealth or occupation; the one-pointed are chief and purify the world.
Having nothing of one's own and relying on the Lord alone (ākiñcanya); being the servant of the Lord's servants; the observances of the vow — no harsh words, no evil tales, alms and help.

relations.note: the Bhāgavata's list of the sādhu's qualities and the Gītā's 'devotee dear to me' cover the same ground

name: The teachers of devotion (bhaktyācāryas)

definitions.definition: NBS 83 names the teachers who with one voice declare devotion supreme: Kumāra, Vyāsa, Śuka, Śāṇḍilya, Garga, Viṣṇu, Kauṇḍinya, Śeṣa, Uddhava, Āruṇi, Bali, Hanumān, Vibhīṣaṇa and others; NBS 16–19 cites the definitions of Vyāsa, Garga, Śāṇḍilya and Nārada; the Śāṇḍilya Sūtra cites Kāśyapa and Bādarāyaṇa.

name: The object of devotion: the Lord as other, the self as one, or both (Śāṇḍilya Sūtra)

definitions.definition: Kāśyapa: devotion is directed to the Lord's majesty, because he is other; Bādarāyaṇa: to the one self; Śāṇḍilya: to both, by scripture and reasoning.

notes: Sūtra wording and numbers recalled with low confidence.

name: The nine exemplars of the nine forms of devotion

definitions.definition: A verse widely quoted in Gauḍīya works names an exemplar for each form: Parīkṣit in hearing, Śuka in singing, Prahlāda in remembering, Lakṣmī in serving the feet, Pṛthu in worship, Akrūra in obeisance, Hanumān in servitude, Arjuna in friendship, Bali in total self-offering.

notes: The verse ('śrī-viṣṇoḥ śravaṇe parīkṣid abhavat ...') is recalled as cited in the Bhaktirasāmṛtasindhu (Eastern division) or the Padyāvalī; exact location not recalled, so no teaching id is created.

name: The divine name (nāma)

definitions.definition: The name 'Nārāyaṇa' is the refuge found after long searching; it gives family, wealth, heaven, grace and strength, more good than a mother; its sweetness is worth more than Indra's kingdom; singing it, past and future faults burn like cotton in fire; by it the senses are guarded and Yama's servants trampled.
Being sung of, the Lord quickly manifests himself and makes his devotees experience him; hearing and singing his qualities are means to devotion even in worldly life.
The Lord himself whispered the eight-syllable mantra into Tirumaṅkai's ear (the tradition's account).

relations.note: the Gauḍīya teaching that even a semblance of the name saves extends the same claim

name: Grace

definitions.definition: The Lord's aruḷ: he graciously gave the Āḻvār knowledge-and-love free of delusion; the Lord came to Tiruppāṇ and Tirumaṅkai unasked; those who recite the Tiruppāvai receive his grace everywhere.
Devotion is gained chiefly by the grace of great souls or a drop of the Lord's grace; even the company of the great is gained by his grace alone.

relations.note: the Gītā's prasāda; same Lord's grace in epic idiom
Tamil aruḷ is also the Śaiva Siddhānta word for Śiva's grace; the Āḻvārs' aruḷ is Tirumāl's — same name, different Lord for each tradition

name: Surrender (prapatti, śaraṇāgati)

definitions.definition: Taking refuge at the Lord's feet with no other refuge, naming Śrī who never leaves his chest (TVM 6.10.10); clinging to the Lord's feet though he cause grief, like a child pushed away that cries for its mother (PT 5.1); giving one's life to the owner of release (TVM 1.2.1); the unbreakable relation pleaded by those with nothing (TP 28).
Having offered self, world and Veda to the Lord, the devotee has no care for worldly loss; self-offering is one of love's eleven forms.

relations.note: the Gītā's 'take refuge in me alone' (18.66)

name: Devotion in separation (viraha)

definitions.definition: The love-sick girl who does not sleep, bails out her tears, joins her palms crying 'conch and discus!' (TVM 7.2.1); Āṇṭāḷ begging for his garment or garland to cool her burning; the grieving father Daśaratha; ended at last in union — Nammāḻvār's longing 'ended' in release.
Supreme anguish at forgetting the Lord is Nārada's own definition of devotion; supreme separation is the last of love's eleven forms.
Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa's mutual longing in separation, carried by the friend, fills most of the Gīta Govinda before union.

name: The Āḻvārs' devotional stances (bhāvas)

definitions.definition: The Āḻvārs approach the Lord as servant (aṭimai, Nammāḻvār), as mother of the child (Periyāḻvār as Yaśodā; Kulaśekhara as Devakī and Kausalyā), as grieving father (Kulaśekhara as Daśaratha), as cowherd companion (the Tiruppāvai girls), as bride and lover (Āṇṭāḷ; Parāṅkuśa- and Parakāla-nāyakī), and as the one who prays for the Lord's own safety (Periyāḻvār's pallāṇṭu).

relations.note: the Āḻvārs' stances answer to the Gauḍīya dāsya, sakhya, vātsalya and madhura rasas, but are not framed as rasas and include the benedictory stance, which the rasa list lacks

name: Bridal love: the devotee as the heroine (nāyikā-bhāva)

definitions.definition: The Āḻvār becomes the girl in love — Parāṅkuśa-nāyakī, Parakāla-nāyakī — spoken of by her mother and friend, sending messengers, threatening to ride the maṭal; Āṇṭāḷ, a woman, sings her own bridal longing and dreams of her wedding.
The gopīs of Vraja are the example of devotion — but their love never lacked knowledge of his greatness and sought his happiness, unlike a paramour's.
Rādhā passes through the heroine's states — waiting, wronged, estranged by pride, going to the tryst, holding her lover in her power.

relations.note: both take the Vraja women's love as the model: the Āḻvārs as poets in Tamil akam voice, the Gauḍīyas as a method of practice following the Vraja residents

name: Tamil love-poetry (akam) and praise-poetry (puṟam) as the language of devotion

definitions.definition: The Āḻvārs cast the soul's love for the Lord in the conventions of Tamil akam poetry — the heroine, her mother and friend, messengers, landscapes, the maṭal — and turn puṟam praise to the Lord's deeds and temples.

name: The Lord's supremacy and his accessibility (paratva, saulabhya)

definitions.definition: The Lord is beyond all, lord of the eternal ones, the cause of Brahmā and the gods; and he is easy of access to those who love him, taking whatever form and name they love, coming as a cowherd and dwelling in temple images.

relations.note: Śrīvaiṣṇava theology lists both among the Lord's auspicious qualities

name: The Lord's subjection to his devotees (bhakta-parādhīnatā)

definitions.definition: The Lord did as his devotee told him, rolling up his serpent-bed; he takes the form his devotees love; the Āḻvār who holds the Lord in his heart asks who is greater.
'I am subject to my devotees, as if not free' (BhP 9.4.63).
Kṛṣṇa pleads to place Rādhā's foot on his head; after union he adorns her at her bidding.

name: The Lord's devotees as one's masters; service to devotees

definitions.definition: The servants of the servants of the Lord, even if caṇḍālas of caṇḍālas, are our masters; brāhmaṇas who revile devotees become outcastes; the Āḻvārs ask to be made servants of the Lord's servants; the Lord made the pāṇar bard be carried into his shrine.

There is no difference between the Lord and his people; among devotees there is no distinction of caste, learning, beauty, family, wealth or occupation, because they are his; the lowest births are eligible for devotion.
A dog-cooker devoted to the Lord is better than a brāhmaṇa with twelve virtues who is averse to him (BhP 7.9.10).

name: Devotion to the teacher as sufficient (ācārya-niṣṭhā)

definitions.definition: Madhurakavi found his teacher by following a light and tested him with a riddle; thereafter saying his teacher's name was sweeter to him than approaching Kṛṣṇa, and he knew no other god; the teacher became mother and father to him. The recitation of this devotion to the teacher is what recovered the Prabandham for Nāthamuni.
Devotion comes chiefly by the grace of great souls, who are not different from the Lord.

relations.note: the disciple's sole reliance on the teacher (niṣṭhā) and the teacher's saving regard (abhimāna) are two sides of the Śrīvaiṣṇava teaching that Madhurakavi's devotion founds

name: The Tamil Veda (Nammāḻvār's works as the four Vedas)

definitions.definition: Nammāḻvār's four works are the four Vedas in Tamil — Tiruviruttam the Ṛg, Tiruvāciriyam the Yajus, Periya Tiruvantāti the Atharva, Tiruvāymoḻi the Sāman — and Tirumaṅkai's six works the six aṅgas; the Tiruvāymoḻi is the Tamil Upaniṣad.
The Āḻvārs call their Tamil the 'Tamil of wisdom' (ñāṉat tamiḻ) and promise the fruit of the Veda to those who recite their decads.

notes: The four-Veda / six-aṅga correspondence is the tradition's account; the source for it is recalled as the Śrīvaiṣṇava commentators and Deśika's Prabandhasāram, not located to a verse.

name: The Āḻvārs' origin: descents of the Lord's attendants, or souls raised by grace

definitions.definition: The hagiographies present the Āḻvārs as descents (aṃśa) of the Lord's weapons, ornaments and attendants — Nammāḻvār of Viṣvaksena, Periyāḻvār of Garuḍa, Kulaśekhara of the Kaustubha, Tirumaḻicai of the discus, Tirumaṅkai of the bow, Āṇṭāḷ of Bhūdevī — and yet also as bound souls to whom the Lord gave knowledge-and-love by grace (TVM 1.1.1).

notes: Aṃśa assignments recalled with low-to-moderate confidence and vary between lists; which Śrīvaiṣṇava teachers stress which reading is not recorded here (see REPORT gaps).

name: The love of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in the Gīta Govinda

definitions.definition: Kṛṣṇa's spring dance with all the cowherd women; Rādhā's jealous withdrawal; the longing of both in separation, carried by the friend; Rādhā's vain waiting and her rebuke; the friend's counsel to give up pride; Kṛṣṇa's plea to place her foot on his head; her going to the tryst; union, and Kṛṣṇa adorning her. The poem offers itself to those who delight in remembering Hari and in the arts of love.

relations.note: the spring dance of GG 1 echoes the rāsa of BhP 10.29–33; Rādhā, unnamed in the Bhāgavata, is central here

notes: The traditions' own warning that the Lord's love-play is not to be imitated by those who are not lords (BhP 10.33.30–31) is the standard caution attached to hearing such poetry (tea:bhagavata-purana:10.33.30-31).

name: The ten descents (daśāvatāra) in the Gīta Govinda

definitions.definition: Fish, tortoise, boar, man-lion, dwarf, Paraśurāma, Rāma, Balarāma, the Buddha (who in compassion condemned animal sacrifice) and Kalki — all forms taken by Kṛṣṇa, to whom the hymn's closing verse bows as the bearer of the ten.

name: Devotees of the Kali age in the Tamil land

definitions.definition: In the Kali age devotees of Nārāyaṇa arise in great numbers in the Draviḍa lands by the Tāmraparṇī, Kṛtamālā, Payasvinī, Kāverī and the western river (BhP 11.5.38–40); the Śrīvaiṣṇava tradition reads this as the Āḻvārs.
With the coming of the dark Lord's singing and dancing devotees the curse on lives is gone, hell laid waste and the Kali age will perish (TVM 5.2.1).

name: Creation, dissolution and the Lord's cosmic deeds in the Āḻvār hymns

definitions.definition: When nothing existed the Lord created Brahmā, gods, worlds and lives; Nārāyaṇa made Brahmā and Brahmā Śiva; he pervades the elements as life in a body; at dissolution he swallows the worlds and lies as a child on a banyan leaf, and restores them; he measured the worlds as Trivikrama.

notes: The banyan-leaf and world-swallowing images are pervasive in the Prabandham; specific verse refs not recorded.

name: Master and servant (śeṣī–śeṣa): the soul's belonging to the Lord

definitions.definition: 'Not knowing myself I thought I and mine; I am yours and what is mine is yours' (TVM 2.9.9); the soul's duty is faultless service at all times (TVM 3.3.1); the Lord stamped the Āḻvār and all his possessions with his discus (PAT 5.4.1).

name: The heart and the senses in the Āḻvār hymns

definitions.definition: The heart-mind (neñcu) is exhorted as a companion to worship and rise, melts with love, and holds the Lord within it; the five senses (aivar) are thieves to be put under guard; the mind of the love-sick girl knows no sleep.

name: The body in the Āḻvār hymns

definitions.definition: The world and elements are the Lord's body, he their life (TVM 1.1.7); the human body is 'impure' and joined to false knowledge (Tiruviruttam 1), yet may be marked as the Lord's (PAT 5.4.1) and, in love, weeps, sleeps not and melts (TVM 7.2.1). The Āḻvār hymns give no teaching on subtle anatomy, channels or centres.

name: The guṇas and devotion

definitions.definition: Secondary devotion is graded by the guṇas; the one who crosses māyā goes beyond the three guṇas; love itself is free of the guṇas.

name: The signs of the lover of God

definitions.definition: Having love, one desires nothing, grieves over nothing, hates nothing, has no zeal for other ends; becomes intoxicated, still, self-delighting; sees, hears, speaks and thinks only of him; with choked voice, bristling hair and tears the one-pointed purify the world.
Sleeplessness, tears bailed out with the hands, joining palms at the names, melting; the love-sick heroine's wasting; the eyes that, having seen him, will see nothing else.
Rādhā in separation makes a bed of flowers that burns her and calls moonlight fire.

name: The devotee's indifference to powers and liberation

definitions.definition: The Āḻvārs want neither Indra's kingdom nor dharma, wealth and pleasure, nor the 'drum' as a reward, but only service and devotion in every birth; the Tiruppallāṇṭu admits seekers of wealth and of self-realisation (kaivalya) only if they give those aims up.
Having gained love one desires nothing and has no zeal for other ends; devotion is higher than action, knowledge and yoga.

name: Keeping scripture and worldly duty after conviction

definitions.definition: Even after conviction becomes firm, scripture is to be kept, lest one fall; worldly conduct continues so far, and eating and the like as long as the body lasts; until love is attained, worldly activity is not abandoned — only its fruit is given up.

name: The last remembrance at death

definitions.definition: Because at death the throat will be choked and remembrance may fail, the devotee hands himself to the Lord now: 'I tell you now, for that hour' (Periyāḻvār); 'let my mind enter your feet this very day' (Mukundamālā).

name: The path of light (arcirādi-gati)

definitions.definition: The ascent of the liberated devotee on the shining path, welcomed by the gods at each stage and received by the eternal ones into the Lord's world (TVM 10.9).

name: Śrī's mediation (puruṣakāra)

definitions.definition: Nammāḻvār surrenders naming Śrī, who cannot part from the Lord even for a moment (TVM 6.10.10); the Tiruppāvai's girls wake Nappiṉṉai to bring them to Kṛṣṇa (TP 16–21); Pēyāḻvār's vision begins 'I have seen Śrī'.

name: Service (kainkarya) as the goal

definitions.definition: 'At all times without break, staying close, we must do faultless service' (TVM 3.3.1); the drum the girls asked for is to be his kin and serve him alone for seven times seven births (TP 29).

name: The 108 divine sites (divya-deśa)

definitions.definition: The temples where the Lord abides in his image, each 'sung' (maṅgaḷāśāsana) by one or more Āḻvārs — 106 on earth with the Milk Ocean and Paramapadam making 108; the Āḻvārs long to be born even as a step or a fish at Tiruvēṅkaṭam and see the Lord at Śrīraṅgam from feet to face.

notes: Regional distribution recalled as Cōḻa 40, Pāṇḍya 18, Malai (Kerala) 13, Naṭu 2, Toṇṭai 22, Vaṭa (north) 11, plus 2 celestial — moderate confidence.
